compensating.why: hop 1 writes the START_OBJECT of the Object itself before passing the field name on
hop 4 moves the parser from the first field name to its value before handing it to the gold
hop 3 copies the current structure itself instead of passing the field name on

expected_signature: Expected token VALUE_NUMBER_INT, current token FIELD_NAME
ownership_reason: Only the gold iterates over the fields of the Object and moves the parser within a field; hop 1 only routes a parser that is not at a field name to copyCurrentStructure, and hops 2-4 pass buffer, parser and context along unchanged. The gold's javadoc promises the fields of the JSON Object copied into the buffer as a single Object, which a stream with every field name written twice is not. No one-line change above the gold restores the stream: moving the parser to the first value before the gold fixes only the first field (the trigger's second field is still written twice), a START_OBJECT written by a hop is a second one, and routing the field-name case to copyCurrentStructure loses the START_OBJECT and stops after one field. The convention is pinned outside the gold by production code doing the same step: AsPropertyTypeDeserializer.deserializeTypedFromObject and BeanDeserializer.deserializeWithUnwrapped read the field name, call jp.nextToken() 'to point to the value', then writeFieldName(name) and copyCurrentStructure(jp); TokenBuffer.copyCurrentStructure on a FIELD_NAME writes the name and moves to the value before copying it. Passing tests: TestVisibleTypeId testVisibleWithProperty ({"a":7, "type":"BaseType"}, the field before the type id buffered by name and value), TestUnwrapped testSimpleUnwrappedDeserialize, TestJacksonTypes testTokenBufferWithSample.
